BiblicalUsage: Chashekah is darkness, and figuratively misery, and it falls on Abram and on the wicked alike. A horror of great darkness fell upon Abram as the sun went down, and God made His covenant with him in it. Isaiah says the rebellious shall look to the earth and behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish, and be driven to darkness. The psalm says the wicked walk on in darkness, and yet the darkness hideth not from God, for the night shineth as the day.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe darkness in these verses is both a place God meets men and a place men hide from Him: Abram's horror came with a covenant, and the wicked's darkness comes with no hiding at all. I hold that the same darkness that terrifies one man comforts another, because God is in it either way.
